met_analysis:
The Depression over Southeast & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 07 kmph during past 06 hours and lies centered at 1730 hours IST of today, the 15th November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 10.2°N and Longitude 86.8°E, about 630 km east-northeast of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 670 km west-southwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman & Nicobar Islands), 780 km east-southeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 920 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 1030 km south-southeast of Gopalpur (Odisha). It is very likely to move north-northwestwards, intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm over the central parts of south & adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal on evening of 16th November and into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal on evening of 17th November, 2026. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further and move northwestwards towards Andhra Pradesh coast during subsequent 2 days.
The east-west trough from the cyclonic circulation associated with the above Depression over Southeast & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal to northern parts of Maldives extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Pakistan & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists with a trough aloft in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along long 72°E to the north of Lat 32°N.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhoodat 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood between 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Sub-Himalayan West Bengal & neighbourhood between 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southeast Arabian Sea off Kerala coast at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
